survey: A cartoon rocket tilted up and to the right, with a sunburst background. Main parts: (1) A red, rounded nose cone that sits on top of the body, with a red rolled rim covering the seam. (2) A silver cylindrical body that narrows slightly toward the tail, facing three-quarters to the camera. (3) Two round portholes with metal rims and blue glass, set flush in the front of the body one above the other. (4) Two red swept fins whose root edges attach along the lower sides of the body, one to the front-left and one to the right. A third fin would be hidden behind the body, so seeing only two fits a three-fin layout. (5) A short black nozzle ring at the tail, centered on the body. (6) A small yellow exhaust flame coming from the nozzle. The rocket is shown in flight, so it needs no ground support. Every part is attached and lined up on the body's axis. The flame is a real part of a working rocket, not an invented one. The squat nozzle is a normal simplification.
